title: A flat finite presentation has a flat finitely presented integer model
statement: Let R and S be commutative rings and f : R → S a finitely presented ring map [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] which is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. There exist commutative rings P and Q, a P-algebra structure on Q and a P-algebra structure on R, such that P is finitely presented over Z, Q is finitely presented over P, P → Q is flat, and there is a ring isomorphism e : R ⊗_P Q ≅ S with e composed with the canonical map R → R ⊗_P Q equal to f. The universes of P and Q may be taken to be the maximum of those of R and S.

proof.text: Use the finite-presentation approximation to write f : R → S as the directed colimit of Pλ → Qλ, with pushout transition and limit squares. Each Pλ is finite type over Z; Qλ is finite type over Pλ. Since Z is Noetherian, both rings are Noetherian and these algebras are finitely presented. If the universes differ, lift the presentations to their common maximum universe; this changes neither their algebraic properties nor their underlying ring maps.

For each λ define Uλ to be the primes q of Qλ where (Qλ)_q is flat over Pλ. Openness follows from the flat-locus theorem applied to the module Qλ, finitely presented over itself. For λ ≤ μ, the localization of Qμ at the image of Qλ minus q is the base change of (Qλ)_q along Pλ → Pμ. It is flat over Pμ by base change; localizing further at any prime above q preserves flatness. Thus the inverse image of Uλ is contained in Uμ.

proof.text: Fix q in Spec S and let p=f inverse(q). Contract these primes to Pλ and Qλ. Their localizations have colimits R_p and S_q and local transition maps. They are Noetherian local rings. Use Nλ=(Qλ)_{qλ}, a cyclic module over its top local ring. Ring transitions are localizations of the base-changed local rings, by the approximation pushout property and localization-tensor compatibility; module transitions are base change of the cyclic top module. Flatness of f implies S_q is flat over R_p. The Noetherian local eventual-flatness result yields some Nλ flat over (Pλ)_{pλ}. Flatness over a localization implies flatness over Pλ, so q lies over Uλ. Persistence then gives membership at every later index.

proof.text: Pull Uλ back to an open subset Vλ of Spec S. These opens are increasing and cover Spec S by the preceding steps. Quasi-compactness gives a finite subcover. Nonemptiness and directedness give a common upper index λ₀ whose Vλ₀ is all of Spec S, also when Spec S is empty.

source.place: Lemma Tag 02JO (lemma-flat-finite-presentation-limit-flat, line 47331), proof of (1), second paragraph ('Since Spec(S) is quasi-compact ...')

proof.text: Write Spec Qλ₀ minus Uλ₀ as V(J). Since its pullback is empty, the image of J generates the unit ideal of S. Express 1 as a finite sum of images of elements of J multiplied by coefficients in S. Represent the coefficients at a common later stage and descend the relation minus 1, which is zero in the colimit, to zero at a further stage. No prime at this stage can contain all these images of J. Every prime therefore contracts into Uλ₀ and lies in its own stage flat locus by persistence.

proof.text: At the stage obtained above all localizations of Q at primes are flat over P. They are modules over the corresponding localizations of P, so the flatness-localization equivalence and the local criterion make P → Q flat. The approximation supplies an isomorphism R ⊗_P Q ≅ S compatible with f. The finite presentations of P over Z and Q over P were established in the first step.
